title_pattern.template: What if You're The Last [casual noun for a group] on Earth?
title_pattern.notes: Classic second-person what-if. 'Guy' instead of 'Man' makes it casual and slightly comic, which signals the tone (dark comedy, not doom). The premise is gendered (only men vanish), and that is only clear from the thumbnail ('4B WOMEN?!'). Title and thumbnail split the job: the title gives the scenario and the thumbnail gives the twist and the stakes. The in-video title card says the formal version: 'WHAT IF YOU WERE THE LAST MAN ON EARTH?'.

thumbnail.composition: Wide 16:9 hotel-corridor scene in the channel's flat 3D style. A large protagonist (faceless black round head, navy suit, cyan tie) on the right tugs his collar with a sweat drop and worried eyes. A woman in a red dress lounges on a bed in the lower-left foreground with heart eyes. Behind them a deep-perspective queue of women with heart eyes stretches down the corridor to a vanishing point.
thumbnail.text: '4B WOMEN?!' top-left in two lines: '4B' in huge white rounded heavy sans, 'WOMEN?!' in yellow with a dark outline. 2 words, number-led.
thumbnail.colours: Saturated royal-blue walls with warm cream corridor light; red dress, pink hearts, yellow text, cyan tie. High-key and warm overall, with complementary blue vs red/yellow accents.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: One big nervous man vs an endless shrinking queue of women: the 1-vs-4-billion ratio is shown as a perspective line. The faceless characters make heart eyes and the sweat drop the only facial read, so the emotion survives at feed size.
thumbnail.why_it_works: The number ('4B') plus the punctuation ('?!') makes the absurd ratio the hook. The visual is a comic 'too much of a good thing' gag (he looks scared, not happy), which promises that the fantasy goes wrong, the same irony as the video's 'What could possibly go wrong?'. Clean shapes and very few colours keep it readable.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: At 9:41, every man on Earth disappears. Bus drivers, boyfriends...
hook.verbatim_0_33s: At 9:41, every man on Earth disappears. Bus drivers, boyfriends, the guy selling hot dogs, gone. Mid-sentence. Every single one, except you. [laughter] Yeah, this is the fantasy every guy has had at least once. That night, you fall asleep smiling. 4 billion women and one of you. What could possibly go wrong?
hook.device: Precise-time cold open ('At 9:41', with an LED clock flipping from 9:40 to 9:41 on screen) + a rapid list of concrete, everyday men, each vanishing on cue in its own 1-2 s shot (man with shopping bag, bus driver, hot dog vendor, boyfriend mid-sentence with a speech bubble cut off at 'So anyway, I was'). Then the stakes on a news ticker (MEN ON EARTH counter crashes from 816,408,931 to 1), the second-person reversal 'except you', and a comic cutaway (the cat caption 'Biscuit is also a boy. He doesn't count.') with a laugh sting. It closes on dramatic irony: 'What could possibly go wrong?' while you dream, then 'Let's see if you keep that energy' pivots to the dark side.
hook.first_frame: Extreme close-up of a green LED pharmacy clock reading 9:40 PM over a blurred night street. It reads as a precise moment before the viewer knows why.

beats.summary: 9:41 PM, city street: men vanish in sparkles mid-action (shopping, driving a bus, selling hot dogs, mid-sentence on a park bench). The News 9 counter drops to MEN ON EARTH: 1.
'Except you.' You on the couch with your cat, plus a caption gag ('Biscuit is also a boy. He doesn't count.'). You smile at the window; laugh sting; freeze-frame polaroid.
Narrator names the fantasy. You fall asleep smiling and dream of a pink garden of heart-eyed women. 'What could possibly go wrong?'

'While you dream, the world is screaming': 4B people vanished, families lost someone, driverless cars crash, planes with no pilot (1 in 20 pilots is a woman), candle vigils. 'Is this the end of humanity?'
LED dot-matrix title: WHAT IF YOU WERE THE LAST MAN ON EARTH?

Chapter sign '1 · THE MORNING AFTER'. Walls of missing posters, then the counter-view: an influencer calls it the best day in history (comment UI gags). Her ring light dies, which turns into the next beat.
Each job men did becomes a failing system with a stat label: grid (96% of line workers), trucks (90%, shelves empty by day 3), ships (99% of sailors), miners, soldiers, 160+ world leaders.
One piece of good news: 2 in 3 health workers are women, so hospitals keep running.
No men means no babies. Sperm banks are empty ('EVERY SAMPLE: GONE'); a population line chart falls to zero over about 100 years. Cliffhanger: 'Unless the last man on Earth gets out of bed.'
'2 · THE LAST BACHELOR'. You wake up feeling like a king (4 years single) and get ready: suit, rose, hair ('close enough'). Mirror practice goes badly; deep breath.
One woman notices, then all of them. Run. Top-down map chase (YOU vs EVERYONE ELSE) and a screeching laundromat encounter. You lose them in an alley.
'Meet Brenda': wig, dress, heels. The police hunting the last man wave at you. A heel catches in a grate; 'IT'S A MAN!' comic burst; 'Lights out.'
'3 · HOPE'. Your arrest photo is on every screen ('LAST MAN ON EARTH FOUND - IN HEELS'), plus merch, a golden statue of you in the dress, and crowds with candles. One-word button: 'Hope.'
You wake chained in a bunker, still in the dress. General Valentina Cross: 'You are humanity's last hope... You can help us or not. Your choice.' You choose to help.
A few months later: VIP life by the pool, robe and attendants. 'But here's the problem.'

'4 · SUPPLY & DEMAND'. 100M sperm a day (1,157/s). The record holder, a Moroccan sultan with ~1,000 kids, needed 1-2 'appointments' a day for 30+ years. 2B women at one a day means 5.5M years (on-screen year counter, THUD faint gag).
Plan B: IVF. One sperm per egg (ICSI), tens of millions per sample, 4M IVF cycles a year, about 1M babies. Every lab on Earth works on Project 001. 'Your new job? Fill a cup and go back to the pool.'

'5 · THE NEXT GENERATION'. Year one: babies in Tokyo, Sao Paulo, Lagos; 'It's a boy'; MEN ON EARTH: 2; global fireworks; 1M babies in year one; clinics scale like factories, reaching 10M babies a year by year 10.
Catch: every child is a half-sibling, so sons marry girls who were kids on the night. Genghis Khan's Y chromosome is in 1 man in 200; here every man carries YOURS.

The world doesn't wait: WWII callback (6M+ American women went to work, 1942), so 'we've still got this'. Women fix the grid and drive the trucks and planes, and the city lights come back. Year 13 puberty gag (choir voice crack).

Year 18: graduation, the first men in two decades, a MEN ON EARTH counter climbing past 50M. 100M+ kids in a 'WE ♥ DAD' stadium, a name wall with 'NAMES REMEMBERED: 2' gag, and 'REBOOTING HUMANITY 16% to 100%'.

'EPILOGUE · THE LAST MAN', 50 years later: statue ('HE SHOWED UP'), World's #1 Dad, Father's Day is basically your birthday. Old you on a rooftop deck chair watches families and traffic. Answers the title question: dream for a night, then the hardest job in history, 'mostly from a deck chair' ('(you're welcome.)').
Music-only end card: poolside set with you in the deck chair, two end-screen video slots and a subscribe circle; kids pile in.

pacing.notes_on_speech: Steady ~130 wpm. It quickens to ~155 wpm in the stats-heavy generation montage (330-420 s) and slows in the comedy set pieces, where visuals carry the jokes (chase, Brenda). Pauses of 2-6 s sit at the comic beats and chapter turns (13 s laugh, 64 s title, 191 s chase, 262 s 'your choice', 341 s chapter 5). 13 s of music-only outro.
pacing.rehook_interval_s: ~20-40 s. Each chapter opens on a diegetic numbered sign and each act ends on a turn line ('What could possibly go wrong?', 'Then her ring light flickers and dies', 'Unless the last man on Earth gets out of bed', 'One problem, you can't walk in heels', 'But here's the problem', 'Here's the catch'). A new number, label or comic burst lands every 3-6 s.
pacing.structure_timing_pct: cold open 0-3% | irony setup 3-7% | global stakes 7-12% | title 12-13% | ch1 consequences + collapse + core problem 13-31% | ch2 bachelor comedy (prep, chase, Brenda) 31-45% | ch3 fame/hope + general's choice 45-55% | ch4 math problem + IVF solution 57-69% | ch5 next generation + genetics + rebuild + reboot 69-89% | epilogue 89-97% | end screen 97-100%

techniques_worth_copying: Precise-time cold open ('At 9:41'), with the clock itself as the first frame. The time comes back as a motif (polaroid 'the night 9:41' at 380 s), so the opening becomes a callback.

A list of vanishing archetypes, one shot each ('Bus drivers, boyfriends, the guy selling hot dogs ... Mid-sentence'). Every noun gets its own 1-2 s visual payoff, and the last one is cut off mid-speech bubble for a laugh.
A persistent MEN ON EARTH counter is the video's spine: 816M to 1 (hook), 1 on vigil banners, 2 at the first birth, 20M to 52M at graduation. One number shows the whole story arc.

Diegetic numbered chapter cards ('1 · THE MORNING AFTER', '2 · THE LAST BACHELOR', '3 · HOPE', '4 · SUPPLY & DEMAND', '5 · THE NEXT GENERATION', 'EPILOGUE · THE LAST MAN') on doors and signs in the world, never full-screen slates. They give long-form structure without breaking immersion.

Stat-per-shot montage: each lost profession is one set (bucket truck, truck depot, ship bridge, mine, summit) with a small monospace pill label giving the stat ('99% OF SAILORS ARE MEN'). Facts land as visual nouns, not voice-over lists.

It alternates hard science with slapstick: every heavy stat block is followed by a comedy set piece (Brenda disguise, THUD faint, CRACK voice break, NAMES REMEMBERED: 2). Long-form what-if keeps retention with a joke every ~30 s.

Second-person protagonist with a faceless round-head avatar plus a pet sidekick (Biscuit). Because the viewer IS 'you', the absurd premise feels personal. Callbacks to the cat and the deck chair close the loop.

Big-number reframes as animated counters with a relatable divisor ('100,000,000 / DAY = 1,157 PER SECOND', '4,097,408 YEARS' counting up, '~1,000 KIDS'). Historical anchors (Moroccan sultan, Genghis Khan 1 in 200, 1942 riveters) make the numbers credible.
Comic-book burst SFX graphics ('IT'S A MAN!', 'THUD', 'CRACK!', 'HONK!', 'SCREECH!') paired with an audio sting. Cheap to make and they punctuate jokes at feed scale.

Ending: answer the title question in one line ('For one night it would feel like a dream. Then it would be the hardest job in human history') then undercut it with the running gag ('mostly from a deck chair'). Circular callback to the opening fantasy.
The thumbnail/title split: the title is the neutral what-if, and the thumbnail carries the hook number and the emotional contradiction (scared man, 4B WOMEN?!).

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: Medium-high. The look is soft-lit low-poly 3D (Blender-style isometric dioramas), which pure SVG cannot match. But almost every shot is a static or slowly-moving diorama with flat characters, labels and counters, so a 2.5D Remotion version with layered SVG sets plus parallax gets 80% of the effect.
code_only_remake_requirements.characters: One rig: a faceless black circle head on a stick body with ellipse eyes and swappable expression states (^^ happy, flat-line deadpan, heart eyes, sweat drop, blush, '!' burst); hair and outfit layers (hoodie, suit, wig + sundress, robe, old-age). Women share the same rig with hair/earring/dress variants. A pet cat sprite. Crowds are instanced tiny rigs (hundreds to thousands; a canvas layer for very large crowds or dot fields).
code_only_remake_requirements.sets: About 25 reusable SVG backdrops: night street with storefronts (Pharmacy, Tony's Pizza, Luna Cafe, Suds & Spin), park bench, apartment interior/window, brick facade with windows (for the long truck), news studio, cockpit, supermarket aisle, ship bridge, mine, summit room, hospital corridor, cryo hall, bunker, poolside resort, lab, nursery, playground, graduation quad, stadium, rooftop at sunset. Day/dusk/night colour grades as palette tokens.
code_only_remake_requirements.graphics_components: LED dot-matrix text component (clock + title card); monospace pill stat labels; animated rolling counters (big serif gold numerals on dark navy panels); line chart (population to zero, bg colour lerp); bar chart; world map and rotating globe with dot/arc overlays; split-screen panels; comic burst stars with text; phone livestream/comment UI; news lower-third + ticker; polaroid freeze-frame; dream/thought bubble mask; diegetic chapter signs (door plaques, hanging signs); end-screen layout.
code_only_remake_requirements.motion: Slow dolly/truck parallax across layered sets (3-5 depth layers), crane up/down by scaling layers, push-ins on characters, whip-pan blur transitions, sparkle-dissolve vanish effect (particle burst + opacity), pop-in labels with spring easing, counters with ease-out roll, pages flipping for the ledger.
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Local TTS narrator (calm, wry male, ~130 wpm) with word timings for label sync; music bed with ducking; SFX library for stings (laugh, screech, thud, crack, honk, whoosh, sparkle). No captions burned in except occasional character lines and asides in italics.
code_only_remake_requirements.data_driven_storyboard: Each beat = {set, characters+expressions, camera move, labels[], counter{from,to}, sfx}. About 55-60 shots for 8 min, an average visual change every 2-3 s inside shots via labels/counters/expression swaps.
code_only_remake_requirements.gaps_vs_original: The original has volumetric lighting, soft shadows, depth of field and real 3D camera moves (orbits around the ship, crane over crowds). Approximate them with gradient lighting overlays, blur on far layers and pre-drawn isometric angles; accept a flatter look or render key 3D shots in Blender separately (the Mac is reserved, so only as a Spark CPU job if allowed).
